_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Government Air Segment (AS) Hardware in the Loop (HITL) System Support Plan (HSSP)
summary: The HSSP describes the Contractor's plan to deliver, install, and support the Government AS HITL system and specifies the Contractor's HITL product deliverables to the Government.
use_relationship: The Government AS Hardware in the Loop (HITL) System Support Plan (HSSP) describes the Contractor's plan to deliver, install, and support the Government AS HITL. The HSSP also specifies the Contractor's HITL product deliverables to the Government. This Data Item Description (DID) contains the format, content, and intended use information for preparation of instructions for the HSSP.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Reference Documents
preparation_instructions.content: The applicable issue of the documents cited herein, including their approval dates and dates of any applicable amendments, notices and revisions, shall be as specified in the contract.

preparation_instructions.title: Format
preparation_instructions.content: The HSSP format may be contractor selected but shall contain all of the Elements discussed below in addition to any other requirements. Unless effective presentation would be degraded, the initially used format shall be used for all subsequent submissions. All updates shall be conspicuously indicated in a manner consistent with standard editorial practices.

preparation_instructions.title: Content
preparation_instructions.content: The AS HSSP will contain the following information:

children.title: Table of contents, list of illustrations, acronyms/abbreviations.
Overview
children.content: Provide the plan's purpose and scope, system description and overall Contractor strategy to accomplish the contract SOW Government HITL tasking.

children.title: Main Body
children.content: Government AS HITL system design, development, integration, test, delivery, installation and life cycle support plans for the program to include, but are not limited to, the following:

children.title: List and description of HITL equipment, racks; breakouts and external interface product deliverables to the Government that include all necessary AS Weapon Replaceable Assemblies (WRAs), cables, emulators or simulators, stimulators and instrumentation required to provide complete AS test and integration capabilities.
List any technical data and computer software, including source code, which the Contractor proposes to deliver, including data rights and licensing requirements.

Plan to connect to the Defense Research & Engineering Network (DREN) as transport and Secret DREN (SDREN), and the Navy Wide Area Network (WAN) for Test and Evaluation (T&E) (NWT&E), where required, to support distributed efforts, to include Live-Virtual-Constructive (LVC) events and rapid data transfer.

Listing of all Information Assurance (IA) artifacts and plan to deliver all IA artifacts, patching, Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M), Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) checklists and system description required to achieve and maintain an Authority to Operate (ATO) via DREN/SDREN and NWT&E.
For all equipment that requires Internet Protocol (IP) addressing, approach to allow for configuration of the addresses.
Plan to communicate to or stimulate AS systems via interfaces such as Radio Frequency (RF), digital, and analog interfaces.

Plan to modify, integrate and/or install simulation-independent middleware software packages, Architecture Management Integration Environment (AMIE plug-ins), Gateways, Adaptors or Interfaces, permitting System Test and Integration Lab (STIL) systems and subsystems to participate in distributed engineering and test efforts.

Plan to limit using proprietary simulations by using Government owned, nonproprietary simulation capabilities such as Navy Portable Source Initiative, (NPSI) and/or, Next Generation Threat System (NGTS).

Approach to demonstrate that the HITL system replicates the AS system/subsystem performance as required by the AS performance specification of this contract, including the Contractor's plan to update, standardize; and maintain revision and change histories of all test procedures; and include requirements traceability matrices or equivalent to map test cases to requirements.
children.content: Automated testing is the preferred method.

children.title: Plan to deliver a Facility Integration and Acceptance Plan.
Plan to deliver Level II drawings and associated lists depicting the designs for the HITL system to the detail necessary for the Government to build and run the simulation and associated equipment.
List documentation deliverables required for the Government to operate and maintain the HITL system and associated equipment.
Specific Government STIL personnel training needs.

Description of how the HITL system design, development, test, documentation and reporting activities will be integrated into its system engineering plans and processes, including the required Systems Engineering Technical Review (SETR) events.

Plan to provide life cycle support for the Government HITL system, including, but not limited to, replacement parts, repairs, maintenance, personnel, hardware/software updates and configuration management.
Approach to HSSP revisions.
